gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on these 2× USB-C + 1× USB-A 65 W travel chargers, the second USB-C port and the USB-A port used together fall to 5 V and 15 W in total. Verbatim's page for the 32201 and D-Link's page for the DCP-651 both say so, which means a laptop has to go in port C1.
standout_why: I compared against the pages I could open. smartgadgetkit.com's UGREEN 90409 review (cited) gives only 45 W + 20 W for two USB-C devices and 45 + 8.5 + 8.5 W for all three, with no C2 + USB-A case and nothing on PPS or Samsung. mobileplustech.com's 65W roundup gives only UGREEN's 45 W + 20 W, gives no pair limits for any model and mentions PPS for none. ChatGPT's own answers state only 45 W + 20 W. Our current page lists D-Link's C+C and C+A splits but not C2 + A. Android Central's page came back cut off after the header and thisusb.com failed on a certificate error, so I could not check either.
decides: This doesn't change the pick, but it adds a 'which port' rule the page lacks. Of the two makers whose pages I could open, Verbatim's 32201 also lists PPS and weighs 105 g against D-Link's 240 g, so it is the better-documented runner-up with US, UK and EU heads. I could not confirm whether UGREEN's 90409 has the same C2 + USB-A drop, because UGREEN's stores returned HTTP 429 every time. The page should say so instead of assuming it.
